definitions.gloss: blanching; briefly passing through hot water
definitions.explanation: a cooking technique where ingredients are briefly dipped in boiling water to soften, remove impurities, or set color

examples.japanese: {刺身|さしみ}を{湯通|ゆどお}しする。
{肉|にく}を{湯通|ゆどお}しして{臭|くさ}みを{取|と}る。
examples.english: Blanch the meat to remove the smell.

examples.japanese: {豆腐|とうふ}は{湯通|ゆどお}ししておくと{崩|くず}れにくい。
examples.english: If you blanch tofu beforehand, it's less likely to fall apart.

notes:
COOKING TECHNIQUE:
{湯通|ゆどお}し involves briefly dipping ingredients in boiling water. The name comes from {湯|ゆ} (hot water) + {通|とお}す (to pass through).

PURPOSES:
- Remove fishy or meaty odors
- Remove excess oil or fat
- Soften texture slightly
- Set color in vegetables
- Firm up delicate ingredients like tofu

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {刺身|さしみ}の{湯通|ゆどお}し - blanching sashimi (creates "tataki" texture)
- {肉|にく}の{湯通|ゆどお}し - removing impurities from meat before cooking
- {野菜|やさい}の{湯通|ゆどお}し - brightening vegetable colors

SIMILAR TECHNIQUES:
- {茹|ゆ}でる - to boil (longer cooking time)
- {下茹|したゆ}で - parboiling (slightly longer than {湯通|ゆどお}し)
- {霜降|しもふ}り - same technique for meat/fish
